statement: A palindrome is a number that reads the same forward and backward, such as $3773$. How many four-digit palindromes are divisible by $11$?

choices.misconception: I used a digit sum test by mistake: I needed the digit sum 2(a + b) to be a multiple of 11, so a + b = 11, which gives only 8 palindromes.
I only counted the palindromes with all four digits the same, 1111, 2222, up to 9999.
I thought a palindrome is divisible by 11 only when its middle digits are even, so I counted half of the 90 palindromes.
I did not allow the middle digits to be 0, so I counted 9 times 9 = 81 and missed palindromes like 3003.

hints: A four-digit palindrome has the form $\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{a}$. How many are there in all?
Use the test for $11$: look at the alternating sum of the digits.
The alternating sum is $a - b + b - a = 0$ for every palindrome of this form.

solutions.reliable: A four-digit palindrome is $\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{a}$ with $a$ from $1$ to $9$ and $b$ from $0$ to $9$, so there are $9 \cdot 10 = 90$ of them. A number is divisible by $11$ when its alternating digit sum is a multiple of $11$, and here that sum is $a - b + b - a = 0$. So every one of the $90$ palindromes is divisible by $11$. For example, $3773 = 11 \cdot 343$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
